name: St. Pierre and Miquelon
rule: Current Code rural L274-12/L271-7 expressly imports a risk-qualified manufactured-plant-product definition, supporting a general-category argument for finished sencha. However, current Ministry instruction 2026-165 expressly includes PM while retaining pre-2019 rules pending a decree, despite the statutory 14 April 2020 longstop. The local 2009 order’s simple-preparation scope and current authorization/certificate provisions must be reconciled; no-document shipment remains unresolved.
personalMailApplicability: The enacted2009 local order expressly covers private and commercial postal/express shipments. The favorable current statutory definition is commodity-based, not a traveller concession. No Japan allowance follows from the Newfoundland-only exception.
authority: French Code rural, Saint Pierre and Miquelon provisions; prefecture
remainingQuestion: Resolve the publicly documented statutory/administrative implementation conflict and the applicable general manufacturing boundary for the local 2009 order. A current published general processing clarification or operative implementation text would suffice; a tea-specific permit letter is not inherently required.
researchAttempts: Reviewed current territory-specific Code rural provisions D274-26 onwards and the prefectural import order; distinguished professional registration and Newfoundland concessions from the Japanese personal postal case.
Second review confirmed current August 2026 Code rural text D274-29 and D274-30: certificate controls and the Newfoundland-only personal exception remain; no processed-sencha ruling found.

30 September bounded legal-scope peer review: Independently retrieved the complete current Code rural D274-26 to D274-31. D274-29 imposes certification on covered plants/plant products generally rather than only an exhaustive commodity list. D274-27/28 have the authorization/application route; D274-26-1 registration is professional only and is not the basis for a private exclusion. D274-30 exempts private imports from Newfoundland, which does not cover a direct Japan parcel. The local 2009 text reproduced in the official 2010 environment report defines products by no/simple processing and explicitly covers postal and express consignments. Thus there is a genuine processing-definition issue, not a missing tea line in an exhaustive schedule.

30 September independent definition review recovered the express L274-12 -> L271-7 -> EUArt2(2) legal chain and full enacted Ordinance 2019-1110. Actual ISPM32 tea Category 1 plus MAFF manufacture is favorable. Coordinated peer recovery of DGAL 2026-165 p4 expressly naming PM reveals current administrative continuation of pre-2019 law against the statutory longstop; preserve the genuine implementation/local-definition conflict rather than require a bespoke ruling. Full notes: wf-pm-definition-review/review-notes.json.
permitFreeReason: Current Code rural L274-12/L271-7 expressly imports a risk-qualified manufactured-plant-product definition, supporting a general-category argument for finished sencha. However, current Ministry instruction 2026-165 expressly includes PM while retaining pre-2019 rules pending a decree, despite the statutory 14 April 2020 longstop. The local 2009 order’s simple-preparation scope and current authorization/certificate provisions must be reconciled; no-document shipment remains unresolved. This is an operative-law conflict, not a rule requiring a bespoke tea classification. ISPM32 tea Category 1 is technical evidence, not an independent domestic waiver.
requiredDocument: Unresolved: applicable plant-product scope and certificate/authorization treatment are not settled by the recovered current sources; ordinary postal/customs declarations alone are not yet verified.

name: Wallis and Futuna
rule: The 2026 French aviation information publication, GEN 1.4.2 for Wallis and Futuna, expressly covers goods and mail. It requires phytosanitary certificates for unmanufactured plant products and exempts loose/bulk tea from the import permit only. It does not establish whether steamed/dried tea in a sealed retail pouch falls within that tea category or outside the unmanufactured-product definition. The traveller processed-food concessions are not a postal exemption.
personalMailApplicability: The published simplified conditions are expressly for arriving travellers. The 100 g tea customs allowance is not evidence of postal agricultural permission.
authority: Wallis and Futuna SIVAP; territorial administration
remainingQuestion: Current binding certificate scope and relation between the specific tea-in-bulk provision and unmanufactured-product definition; full current territorial plant-health consolidation or a published general manufactured-food postal rule. No contrary certificate exemption was established.
researchAttempts: Read SIVAP import/declaration guidance and the referenced local phytosanitary regime.
Read the official traveller sheet and distinguished its exemptions from postal imports.
Searched for tea-specific postal and processed-food conditions; no applicable affirmative rule found.

Read indexed official 2026 AIP GEN 1.4-4, section 1.4.2, which explicitly covers goods and mail. Its tea-in-bulk exception removes only the permit, not the certificate; finished retail tea’s classification remains ambiguous.
Checked the phytosanitary arrival-form update effective January 2026; it is expressly handed to airline passengers and provides no postal certificate exemption.
Searched for current local Order 93-275 amendments or a retail-tea postal clarification; no applicable published clarification was located.

30 September bounded legal-scope peer review: The current accessible AIP section includes mail. Its French wording covers living plants/parts and non-manufactured plant products, then expressly exempts tea in bulk from the import permit alone. It does not waive the phytosanitary certificate for that category. A sealed retail pouch does not by itself prove that loose tea is outside the tea-in-bulk expression; conversely, the specific tea exception makes it unsafe to infer that every manufactured tea is entirely outside scope. The retail/manufactured distinction remains unresolved in this text. Traveller sheets use an arrival declaration and cannot independently supply a postal waiver.

30 September independent definition review recovered SPREP 2022 full comparative report; existing-law column reproduces 95-245 Arts2–3 and default prior-permit waiver but no certificate waiver. Proposed new biosafety sections were not treated as enacted. Official Gazette 714, May 2025 indexedtext calls further import/export sections future proposals. Actual sencha manufacture and ISPM32 are favorable factual evidence; specific tea-in-bulk permit-only entry still prevents clean postal certificate exclusion. See wf-pm-definition-review/review-notes.json.
permitFreeReason: Sencha’s processing and ISPM32 support the factual manufactured/nonliving classification. However, the explicit loose/bulk tea permit-only provision makes WF different from a jurisdiction with only a generic risk definition. A sealed retail pouch does not prove loose leaves are outside the tea-in-bulk expression. Traveller allowances do not settle mail. Current binding certificate scope and relation between the specific tea-in-bulk provision and unmanufactured-product definition; full current territorial plant-health consolidation or a published general manufactured-food postal rule. No contrary certificate exemption was established.
